nodes.title: Stopping distance
nodes.description: know that the stopping distance of a vehicle is made up of the sum of the thinking distance and the braking distance

nodes.title: Half-life
nodes.description: know the definition of the term half-life and understand that it is different for different radioactive isotopes

nodes.title: Core practical 8: investigating thermal energy
nodes.description: Core practical 8: investigate thermal energy transfer by conduction, convection and radiation

nodes.title: Chain reactions
nodes.description: describe how a chain reaction can be set up if the neutrons produced by one fission strike other U-235 nuclei

nodes.title: Differences in orbits
nodes.description: describe the differences in the orbits of comets, moons and planets

nodes.title: Fission
nodes.description: understand how a nucleus of U-235 can be split (the process of fission) by collision with a neutron, and that this process releases energy as kinetic energy of the fission products

nodes.title: The wave equation
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between the speed, frequency and wavelength of a wave: 
wave speed = frequency × wavelength 
v = f × λ

nodes.title: Contamination & irradiation
nodes.description: describe the difference between contamination and irradiation

nodes.title: Uses of radioactivity
nodes.description: describe uses of radioactivity in industry and medicine

nodes.title: Decay equations
nodes.description: understand how to balance nuclear equations in terms of mass and charge

nodes.title: Types of forces
nodes.description: identify different types of force such as gravitational or electrostatic

nodes.title: Core practical 1: investigating motion
nodes.description: Core practical 1: investigate the motion of everyday objects such as toy cars or tennis balls

nodes.title: Absolute zero
nodes.description: understand why there is an absolute zero of temperature which is –273 °C

nodes.title: Advantages & disadvantages
nodes.description: explain why a series or parallel circuit is more appropriate for particular applications, including domestic lighting

nodes.title: Acceleration
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between acceleration, change in velocity and time taken:       

a = (v − u) / t

nodes.title: Elastic behaviour
nodes.description: describe elastic behaviour as the ability of a material to recover its original shape after the forces causing deformation have been removed

nodes.title: Fusion in stars
nodes.description: know that fusion is the energy source for stars

nodes.title: The pressure law
nodes.description: use the relationship between the pressure and Kelvin temperature of a fixed mass of gas at constant volume:  P1 /T1 = P2 / T2

nodes.title: Resistance
nodes.description: describe the qualitative effect of changing resistance on the current in a circuit

nodes.title: Convection
nodes.description: explain the role of convection in everyday phenomena

nodes.title: Video Energy Transfer Pathways
nodes.description: nan

nodes.title: Electromagnetism
nodes.description: know that an electric current in a conductor produces a magnetic field around it

nodes.title: Sankey diagrams
nodes.description: describe a variety of everyday and scientific devices and situations, explaining the transfer of the input energy in terms of the above relationship, including their representation by Sankey diagrams

nodes.title: Atomic & mass number
nodes.description: know the terms atomic (proton) number, mass (nucleon) number

nodes.title: Background radiation
nodes.description: explain the sources of background (ionising) radiation from Earth and space

nodes.title: Reducing energy loss
nodes.description: explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfer, such as insulation

nodes.title: Detecting radiation
nodes.description: know that photographic film or a Geiger−Müller detector can detect ionising radiations

nodes.title: The law of magnetism
nodes.description: know that magnets repel and attract other magnets and attract magnetic substances

nodes.title: Thermal radiation
nodes.description: explain how emission and absorption of radiation are related to surface and temperature

nodes.title: Conduction
nodes.description: describe how thermal energy transfer may take place by conduction, convection and radiation

nodes.title: Products of fission
nodes.description: know that the fission of U-235 produces two radioactive daughter nuclei and a small number of neutrons

nodes.title: Resistors in series
nodes.description: calculate the currents, voltages and resistances of two resistive components connected in a series circuit

nodes.title: Planets, stars & galaxies
nodes.description:
know that: 
•        the universe is a large collection of billions of galaxies
•        a galaxy is a large collection of billions of stars
•        our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy.

nodes.title: The gas laws
nodes.description:
explain, for a fixed amount of gas, the qualitative relationship between: 
•        pressure and volume at constant temperature
•        pressure and Kelvin temperature at constant volume.

nodes.title: Electrical safety
nodes.description: understand how the use of insulation, double insulation, earthing, fuses and circuit breakers protects the device or user in a range of domestic appliances

nodes.title: The life cycle of solar mass stars
nodes.description:
describe the evolution of stars of similar mass to the Sun through the following stages: 
•        nebula
•        star (main sequence)
•        red giant
•        white dwarf.

nodes.title: Critical angle
nodes.description: explain the meaning of critical angle c

nodes.title: Isotopes
nodes.description: know the term isotope

nodes.title: Fusion
nodes.description: describe nuclear fusion as the creation of larger nuclei resulting in a loss of mass from smaller nuclei, accompanied by a release of energy

nodes.title: Factors affecting stopping distance
nodes.description: describe the factors affecting vehicle stopping distance, including speed, mass, road condition and reaction time

nodes.title: Classification of stars
nodes.description: understand how stars can be classified according to their colour. Know that a star’s colour is related to its surface temperature

nodes.title: Fleming's left-hand rule
nodes.description: use the left-hand rule to predict the direction of the resulting force when a wire carries a current perpendicular to a magnetic field

nodes.title: Ray diagrams
nodes.description: draw ray diagrams to illustrate reflection and refraction

nodes.title: Work, GPE & KE
nodes.description: understand how conservation of energy produces a link between gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy and work

nodes.title: Pressure in liquids
nodes.description: understand how the pressure at a point in a gas or liquid at rest acts equally in all directions

nodes.title: Alpha, beta, gamma & neutron emission
nodes.description: describe the effects on the atomic and mass numbers of a nucleus of the emission of each of the four main types of radiation (alpha, beta, gamma and neutron radiation)

nodes.title: Scalar & vector quantities
nodes.description: understand how vector quantities differ from scalar quantities

nodes.title: Calculating half-life
nodes.description: use the concept of the half-life to carry out simple calculations on activity, including graphical methods

nodes.title: Current in series circuits
nodes.description: understand how the current in a series circuit depends on the applied voltage and the number and nature of other components

nodes.title: Thermistors & LDRs
nodes.description: describe the qualitative variation of resistance of light-dependent resistors (LDRs) with illumination and thermistors with temperature

nodes.title: Calculating uniform acceleration
nodes.description:
use the relationship between final speed, initial speed, acceleration and distance moved: 
(final speed)2 = (initial speed)2 + (2 × acceleration × distance moved) 

v2 = u2 + (2 × a × s)

nodes.title: Calculating pressure in a liquid
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship for pressure difference: 
pressure difference = height × density × gravitational field strength p = h × ρ × g

nodes.title: Core practical 13: investigating radiation
nodes.description: Core practical 13: investigate the penetration powers of different types of radiation using either radioactive sources or simulations

nodes.title: The Kelvin scale
nodes.description: describe the Kelvin scale of temperature and be able to convert between the Kelvin and Celsius scales

nodes.title: Activity & decay
nodes.description: know that the activity of a radioactive source decreases over a  period of time and is measured in becquerels

nodes.title: Effects of forces
nodes.description: describe the effects of forces between bodies such as changes in speed, shape or direction

nodes.title: The Doppler effect
nodes.description: explain why there is a change in the observed frequency and wavelength of a wave when its source is moving relative to an observer, and that this is known as the Doppler effect

nodes.title: Calculating critical angle
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between critical angle and refractive index: 
sin c = 1 / n

nodes.title: Total internal reflection
nodes.description: describe the role of total internal reflection in transmitting information along optical fibres and in prisms

nodes.title: Magnetic materials
nodes.description: describe the properties of magnetically hard and soft materials

nodes.title: Nuclear energy
nodes.description: know that nuclear reactions, including fission, fusion and radioactive decay, can be a source of energy

nodes.title: Unbalanced forces
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between unbalanced force, mass and acceleration: force = mass × acceleration 
F = m × a

nodes.title: Gravitational potential energy
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between gravitational potential energy, mass, gravitational field strength and height: 
gravitational potential energy = mass × gravitational field strength × height GPE = m × g × h

nodes.title: Forces as vectors
nodes.description: understand that force is a vector quantity

nodes.title: The conditions for fusion
nodes.description: explain why nuclear fusion does not happen at low temperatures and pressures, due to electrostatic repulsion of protons

nodes.title: Voltage in series & parallel
nodes.description: know that the voltage across two components connected in parallel is the same

nodes.title: Applications of EM waves
nodes.description:
explain some of the uses of electromagnetic radiations, including: 
•        radio waves: broadcasting and communications
•        microwaves: cooking and satellite transmissions
•        infrared: heaters and night vision equipment
•        visible light: optical fibres and photography
•        ultraviolet: fluorescent lamps
•        x-rays: observing the internal structure of objects and materials, including for medical applications
•        gamma rays: sterilising food and medical equipment.

nodes.title: Fusion vs fission
nodes.description: explain the difference between nuclear fusion and nuclear fission

nodes.title: Video of the Life Cycle of Low-Mass Stars
nodes.description: nan

nodes.title: Gravitational field strength
nodes.description: understand why gravitational field strength, g, varies and know that it is different on other planets and the Moon from that on the Earth

nodes.title: Kinetic energy
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship: 
kinetic energy =  1/2 × mass × speed2 
KE = 1 / 2 × m× v

nodes.title: Properties of radiation
nodes.description: describe the nature of alpha (α) particles, beta (β−) particles, and gamma (γ) rays, and recall that they may be distinguished in terms of penetrating power and ability to ionise

nodes.title: Reflection & refraction
nodes.description: explain that all waves can be reflected and refracted

nodes.title: Terminal velocity
nodes.description: describe the forces acting on falling objects (and explain why falling objects reach a terminal velocity)

nodes.title: Hooke's law
nodes.description: know that the initial linear region of a force-extension graph is associated with Hooke’s law

nodes.title: Lamps & LEDs
nodes.description: know that lamps and LEDs can be used to indicate the presence of a current in a circuit

nodes.title: Electromagnetic induction
nodes.description: know that a voltage is induced in a conductor or a coil when it moves through a magnetic field or when a magnetic field changes through it and describe the factors that affect the size of the induced voltage

nodes.title: Current in parallel circuits
nodes.description: understand why current is conserved at a junction in a circuit

nodes.title: AC & DC
nodes.description: know the difference between mains electricity being alternating current (a.c.) and direct current (d.c.) being supplied by a cell or battery

nodes.title: Factors affecting magnetic force
nodes.description: describe how the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field changes with the magnitude and direction of the field and current

nodes.title: Calculating average speed
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between average speed, distance moved and time taken:

average speed = distance moved/time taken

nodes.title: Energy stores & transfers
nodes.description:
describe energy transfers involving energy stores: 
•        energy stores: chemical, kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear
•        energy transfers: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation
(light and sound)

nodes.title: Shielding
nodes.description: understand the role of shielding around a nuclear reactor

nodes.title: The life cycle of larger stars
nodes.description: describe the evolution of stars with a mass larger than the Sun

nodes.title: Atomic structure
nodes.description: describe the structure of an atom in terms of protons, neutrons and electrons and use symbols such as 14/6  c to describe particular nuclei

nodes.title: Core practical 12: investigating magnetic fields
nodes.description: Core practical 12: investigate the magnetic field pattern for a permanent bar magnet and between two bar magnets

nodes.title: Frequency & time period
nodes.description:
use the relationship between frequency and time period: frequency = 1  /  time period 
f  = 1 / T

nodes.title: The law of reflection
nodes.description: use the law of reflection (the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection)

nodes.title: Orbital motion
nodes.description:
explain that gravitational force: 
•        causes moons to orbit planets
•        causes the planets to orbit the Sun
•        causes artificial satellites to orbit the Earth
•        causes comets to orbit the Sun.

nodes.title: Core practical 2: investigating force & extension
nodes.description: Core Practical 2: investigate how extension varies with applied force for helical springs, metal wires and rubber bands

nodes.title: Calculating orbital period
nodes.description:
use the relationship between orbital speed, orbital radius and time period: 
orbital speed = 2 x π x orbital radius / time period
v = 2 x π × r / T

nodes.title: Efficiency
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between efficiency, useful energy output and total energy output: 
efficiency = useful energy output / total energy output × 100%

nodes.title: Control rods & moderators
nodes.description: describe the role played by the control rods and moderator in the fission process

nodes.title: Kinetic theory of gases
nodes.description: explain how molecules in a gas have random motion and that they exert a force, and hence a pressure, on the walls of a container

nodes.title: Boyle's law
nodes.description:
use the relationship between the pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature: 
p1 V1 = p2 V2

nodes.title: IV graphs
nodes.description: describe how current varies with voltage in wires, resistors, metal filament lamps and diodes, and how to investigate this experimentally

nodes.title: Magnetic force on a current-carrying wire
nodes.description: understand why a force is exerted on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field, and how this effect is applied in simple d.c. electric motors and loudspeakers

nodes.title: Calculations in different contexts
nodes.description: use the above relationships in different contexts including sound waves and electromagnetic waves

nodes.title: Generators & dynamos
nodes.description: describe the generation of electricity by the rotation of a magnet within a coil of wire and of a coil of wire within a magnetic field, and describe the factors that affect the size of the induced voltage

nodes.title: Distance-time graphs
nodes.description: plot and explain distance−time graphs

nodes.title: Area under a velocity-time graph
nodes.description: determine the distance travelled from the area between a velocity−time graph and the time axis

nodes.title: Dangers of radiation
nodes.description:
describe the dangers of ionising radiations, including: 
•        that radiation can cause mutations in living organisms
•        that radiation can damage cells and tissue
•        the problems arising from the disposal of radioactive waste and how the associated risks can be reduced.

nodes.title: Types of radiation
nodes.description: know that alpha (α) particles, beta (β−) particles, and gamma (γ) rays are ionising radiations emitted from unstable nuclei in a random process

nodes.title: Permanent & induced magnets
nodes.description: know that magnetism is induced in some materials when they are placed in a magnetic field

nodes.title: Representing magnetic fields
nodes.description: describe how to use two permanent magnets to produce a uniform magnetic field pattern

nodes.title: Gradient of a velocity-time graph
nodes.description: determine acceleration from the gradient of a velocity−time graph

nodes.title: Velocity-time graphs
nodes.description: plot and explain velocity-time graphs

nodes.title: Magnetic field lines
nodes.description: understand the term magnetic field line

nodes.title: Temperature & kinetic energy
nodes.description: know that the Kelvin temperature of a gas is proportional to the average kinetic energy of its molecules

nodes.title: Temperature & speed
nodes.description: understand why an increase in temperature results in an increase in the average speed of gas molecules

nodes.title: Weight
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between weight, mass and gravitational field strength: weight = mass × gravitational field strength 
W = m × g

nodes.title: Conservation of energy
nodes.description: use the principle of conservation of energy
